channel.title: The Dig — Control electronics and cryogenics
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Control electronics and cryogenics preset. Today’s ranked reading list centers on near-term spin-qubit QPU readout, compilation, and control, led by 2611.23448 on ADC-less cryogenic readout, 2611.22315 on connectivity-aware routing and resynthesis, and 2611.24886 on calibration- and noise-aware superconducting compilation; the remaining skims broaden the fault-tolerant and QEC context through 2611.24328 on real-time Pauli-frame tracking, 2611.23919 on minimal-control fault-tolerant architectures, 2611.23009 on dual-rail compilation, 2611.23420 on high-rate low-distance color codes, and 2611.23528 on singlet-flag shuttled qLDPC codes in silicon. item.title: Compute Before You Digitize: ADC-less Mixed-Signal Processing for Scalable Cryogenic Qubit Readout
item.description:
Read new result — DIRAC eliminates Nyquist-rate ADCs via analog demodulation and ping-pong integration, using 50.3 pJ per qubit per readout (31.6× below fixed-point and 238× below FP32). Total 4 K quantum-classical interface power drops to 0.85 mW per physical qubit, a 50.4% reduction versus fixed-point digital baseband.

Grade 0.541 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Engineering the quantum-classical interface of solid-state qubits” · Qirui Zhang, Ben Toby, He Wang, Benjamin Lienhard, David Blaauw, Dennis Sylvester

Figure

Stacked bars of 4 K quantum-classical interface power per physical qubit (mW) broken down by subsystem across FP32, fixed-point, and DIRAC implementations, along with room-temperature flex and coaxial cable heat comparisons.

Asks

Can an in-cryostat readout receiver combine frequency-multiplexed qubit readout with neural network discrimination while reducing 4 K power below room-temperature cable loads?

Before

Conventional cryo-CMOS fixed-point digital baseband with 500 MS/s ADCs consumed 1.59 nJ per qubit burst energy (1.71 mW total 4 K power per physical qubit), saving only 36.7% power over room-temperature electronics with flex cables.

But

Evaluated on 1.12M experimental shots via behavioral models validated against transistor-level simulations over ten mismatch-sampled chips. Requires transmitter/receiver co-design with access to baseband NCO sign bits.

Tools

passive complex mixers · ping-pong active-RC integrators · voltage-to-pulse time-to-digital converters · TX-derived local oscillator reuse · joint matched-filter and neural network training · 22 nm FD-SOI cryo-CMOS at 4 K

Abstract

We introduce DIRAC, an ADC-less in-cryostat qubit readout architecture that uses analog computing to redraw the analog-digital boundary. Directly operating on the front-end's analog output, passive complex mixers perform the equivalent of digital demodulation, ping-pong active-RC integrators average their outputs into down-sampled per-qubit traces, and a time-domain stage digitizes them, eliminating Nyquist-rate ADCs. A TX-RX co-design derives the mixers' local oscillators from the readout transmitter's baseband rather than per-tone PLLs. A per-line calibration flow trains the matched filter jointly with the neural network, improving fidelity and enabling low-bit-width, low-voltage digital processing. Designed in 22 nm FD-SOI and evaluated at 4 K on 1.12M experimental shots, DIRAC matches the fidelity of a floating-point (FP32) digital pipeline for readout windows down to 750 ns, at 31.6× and 238× lower energy than the fixed-point (FxP) and FP32 pipelines. It cuts the total 4 K power per physical qubit by 50.4% and 68.6% relative to FxP and room-temperature flex cables, respectively. At a fixed logical-qubit count and 4 K budget, this yields, against FxP, a code distance larger by 2 to 6 and a 1.6-7.3× (Willow) and 4.9-204× (SI1000, p = 10⁻³) lower logical error rate.
